dod_intent_evidence: Own news posts: awarded a Navy SBIR Phase I ($236,426, contract N6833523C0679, NAVAIR/NAVSEA) and a two-year Phase II SBIR (announced June 2025) to 'develop and demonstrate AI-enabled, automated imagery intelligence software' — an active DoD acquisition motion distinct from their commercial/wildfire business.
score_evidence: 'awarded a Phase II Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract by the U.S. Navy (USN)... Under the two-year Phase II' → stage_pressure (funded-months clock now running against 2026 date)
'Trusted and Deployed Globally Since 2016' and 'Fielded, Proven, Mission-Ready Technology' → lab_language_intensity is low, this is fielding-first messaging
'developed in collaboration with operators and refined through real-world missions' → operator_absence is very low, operators are central to their own narrative

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims 'Integration with existing C2 architectures' but never names ATAK/TAK once, despite delivering ISR intelligence directly to tactical operators.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If ASO's outputs don't speak native TAK/ATAK, the operator has to manually bridge formats in the field — exactly the kind of last-mile integration gap that kills adoption even when the sensor and AI work perfectly.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's fielding history is largely commercial/civil (wildfire, law enforcement, maritime) where TAK isn't the standard; the Navy SBIR work is newer and may not have hit that integration point yet.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/CMMC language anywhere despite active NAVAIR/NAVSEA SBIR contracts that will need to move AI-processed sensor data onto Navy networks.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The AI/ML sensor-video processing described in the SBIR abstract has to get an Authority to Operate before NAVAIR fields it on an actual platform; the Phase II announcement talks about 'developing and demonstrating' the capability but says nothing about the accreditation path that decides whether Phase III ever happens.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Press releases and product pages are written for commercial/investor audiences, not the acquisition compliance process running in parallel on the Navy side.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: awarded a Phase II Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract by the U.S. Navy (USN) to develop and demonstrate AI-enabled, automated imagery intelligence software

blind_spots.blind_spot: No published SWaP-C numbers for the edge AI compute running ASO's real-time computer vision on a gimbal-mounted airborne sensor.
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Edge-based, AI-enabled autonomy' doing real-time detection draws real power and generates real heat on a small airborne platform; without published SWaP figures, an integrator can't confirm ASO fits their platform's power/weight budget until late in integration — the classic point programs stall.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Marketing emphasizes capability outcomes (superhuman vision, workload reduction) over the hardware constraints that gate actual platform integration.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: edge-based, AI-enabled autonomy to ISR workflows

opener_hook: Overwatch Imaging's Navy Phase II SBIR (announced June 2025, contract N6833523C0679) is a two-year clock to demonstrate AI-enabled ISR sensor processing — the announcement describes the capability but not the ATO path that decides whether it survives past Phase II.
what_they_do: Makes AI-enabled airborne ISR smart sensors and Automated Sensor Operator (ASO) software for EO/IR gimbals, fielded commercially worldwide since 2016, now running a Navy SBIR Phase II to extend AI/ML sensor-video processing for DoD use.
